items.weakness_text: Lack of proper acknowledgement of closely related work.
items.ac_evidence: The authors also corrected the major omission around HyperLM by adding explicit positioning and head-to-head comparisons, which reviewer QfN2 indicated was the key condition for recommending acceptance.

items.weakness_text: The paper repeatedly claims to be the "first" to propose a foundation model for label aggregation, and to introduce a new paradigm. Given the existence of[1], these claims are overstated.
Given the existence of the hyper label model approach[1], the main contribution of the paper seems to be modifications to the synthetic data generator and GNN architecture.
items.ac_evidence: Concerns still outstanding or only partially resolved are that the work may still read as incremental depending on how convincingly it is framed as an extension of the HyperLM paradigm rather than a new shift

items.weakness_text: The paper lacks a systematic quantitative analysis of synthetic and real-world crowdsourced data.
items.ac_evidence: the need for stronger evidence that the synthetic generator matches real crowdsourcing behavior (the authors added sim-to-real quantification)

items.weakness_text: the paper lacks a sensitivity analysis of key parameters.
items.ac_evidence: missing ablations and hyperparameter/sensitivity analysis (the authors added both)

items.weakness_text: statistical tests are needed in the comparison results.
items.ac_evidence: lack of statistical rigor in the multi-dataset comparisons (the authors added significance tests)

items.weakness_text: The paper lacks ablation studies to verify the individual contributions of key components.
items.ac_evidence: missing ablations and hyperparameter/sensitivity analysis (the authors added both)

items.weakness_text: How can we ensure that the distribution of synthetic data is sufficient to cover the feature space of real crowdsourcing tasks? Is there any performance degradation under certain types of tasks (such as extremely unbalanced ones)?
items.ac_evidence: there remains some uncertainty about how broadly the synthetic generator’s coverage supports real-world generalization

items.weakness_text: Can CrowdFM be regarded as the specialization of GraphFM in the field of crowdsourcing? Has the pre-training objective of the existing GFM been borrowed?
The performance for extremely large-scale data (such as Senti and Fact) slightly decreases, but the reasons are not discussed.
items.ac_evidence: limited when/why it fails analysis for atypical or very large datasets

items.weakness_text: The absence of ablation experiments makes the contributions of each module unclear
items.ac_evidence: missing ablations and hyperparameter/sensitivity analysis (the authors added both)

items.weakness_text: Although it includes recent works such as EBCC, GOVERN, TiReMGE, etc., some new methods for 2024-2025 are missing (such as Zhang et al., KFNN and IWBVT of NeurIPS 2024 are cited but not used as baselines);
items.ac_evidence: Baseline coverage remains debatable because some suggested recent methods were excluded as “not comparable”

items.weakness_text: The superparameters such as the number of layers L and dimension d of GNN were not discussed in detail.
items.ac_evidence: missing ablations and hyperparameter/sensitivity analysis (the authors added both)

items.weakness_text: The "Sim-to-Real Gap" between synthetic data and real data has not been fully quantified
items.ac_evidence: the need for stronger evidence that the synthetic generator matches real crowdsourcing behavior (the authors added sim-to-real quantification)

items.weakness_text: Has the model truly learned the "principle of collective intelligence", or has it merely fitted the statistical patterns of synthetic data? How to prove.
items.ac_evidence: but baseline coverage/comparability and the strength of the “learned principle” claim still leave it borderline

items.weakness_text: The possible limitation of the model is it may lack the flexibility to adapt to the case when workers/tasks have their attributes, since these nodes are initialized with fixed pretrained embeddings.
items.ac_evidence: real-world applicability remains uncertain in settings where domain/task features or worker/task attributes matter (not directly evaluated)

items.weakness_text: Another possible weakness is the limitation of the data generator. Although it is a quite general scheme, there might be other graphical models that it cannot cover; and also the prior distribution of the parameters might cause some bias for the pretrained foundation model.
items.ac_evidence: there remains some uncertainty about how broadly the synthetic generator’s coverage supports real-world generalization
